To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are significant differences between bipolar disorder (BD) and schizophrenia (SZ) in the trisynapathic pathway in human hippocampus that are consistent with the hypothesis that these disorders have different etiologies and pathophysiological mechanisms.

1) the GABAergic circuitry in the human hippocampus is regulated by a complex network of transcription factors that are differentially regulated in schizophrenia versus bipolar disorder, 2) the transcription factors that are dysregulated are likely to be involved in the development of the GABAergic cells in the trisynapthic pathway, and 3) these transcription factors are likely to be regulated by the extrinsic afferent fibers of the trisynchaptic pathway.

the cellular endo-phenotypes for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder may be determined by unique susceptibility genes for each disorder as well as by altered integration among hippocampus GABA cells with their extrinsic and intrinsic inputs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GABAergic interneurons in the hippocampal circuitry of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and the molecular and genetic mechanisms that regulate these cells.
the identification and characterization of molecular markers that can be used to define cellular endophenotypic profiles for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
how the hippocampal circuit is regulated and how it may be disrupted in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABA cells of CA3/CA2 and CA1 in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder show evidence of reduced numbers of GABAergic neurons and/or reduced GABAergic activity.
the hippocampal GAD67 mRNA expression profile in SZ and BD is not the same, and that there is a unique profile for each disorder.

there is a reduction in the total number of GABA interneurons in the hippocampal formation, and that there is a selective loss in the number of interneuron subpopulations in the trisynaptically projecting GABA cells of SZ and BD subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hippocampus is an important site for studying the pathophysiology of schizophrenia, and that the trisynptic pathway is a useful model for understanding the cellular and molecular basis of the disorder.
the trisynapthic pathway is regulated by a combination of factors that include unique genes, cell types and circuitry.

the hippocampal circuitry-based gene expression profiling in schizophrenia and bipolar disorders is likely to be regulated by multiple factors that includes unique susceptibility genes for each disorder, and altered integration among the hippocampal Gaba cells with extrinsic afferent fiber system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampus in SZ and BD is not simply “dysfunctional”, but rather, the circuitry that is involved in memory and cognition is reorganized in these disorders.
the trisynaptically-projected hippocampal GABAs may be a useful biomarker for the diagnosis of SZ and BD.
the trisynapthic pathway is not a simple, linear pathway, but is a highly integrated and complex circuit, which is subject to multiple regulatory influences.
